De kerk staat op de plek waar Tongelre a: The church stands where Tongelre has gathered round a church since the thirteenth century: on the high ground along the Dommel, on the inner bend of 't Hofke. The present church is a three-aisled neo-Gothic cruciform basilica; the two towers that were to flank the main portal were never finished, so the front stayed low and the nave looks all the longer. The parsonage is attached under the same roof; on its front is a Good Shepherd by the Eindhoven sculptor Jan Custers, 1918.
Op 1 januari 1920 werden Tongelre, Strat: On 1 January 1920 Tongelre, Stratum, Gestel, Strijp and Woensel were joined to the small town of Eindhoven, which needed room: Eindhoven then had 6,500 inhabitants, Tongelre 3,200. This building of 1911 was the last town hall of Tongelre. Both the villagers and the council were against the annexation: they feared higher taxes, a village swallowed by the city, and more crime. It made no difference. The building still serves the neighbourhood.
Een van de oudste panden van Eindhoven,: One of the oldest buildings in Eindhoven, from 1584: a three-aisled hall house with a broad middle aisle and two narrow side aisles, house and stable under one roof. Around 1600 a raised room with a cellar was added; in the eighteenth century the end wall, the street front and the stable were renewed. The farm stood right on Tongelre's village square, long since gone, next to the town hall. An excavation in 1993 found a refuse pit beside it with seventeenth-century Delftware and stained glass.
De pastorie van vóór de huidige kerk, ui: The parsonage from before the present church, from the end of the eighteenth century, on the outer bend of 't Hofke.
Een zestiende-eeuws huis aan de oude weg: A sixteenth-century house on the old road to Urkhoven, where a tanner lived and worked. It stands at the edge of the village core, where the road to Zesgehuchten began.
Hier stond in 1375 al 'Het goed Ten Hove: 'Het goed Ten Hove' stood here as early as 1375, and in 1637 a brick house called Musberg. Jonkheer Smits-van Eckart bought it in 1846 and had the country house and the farm pulled down in 1872 and rebuilt larger; because the complex looked like a castle, it became known as the little castle of Tongelre. Philips bought it in 1920 to build housing, demolished it in 1930, and in 1941 put up a farm after all: the Philips farm. The foundations of the old country house still lie under the sand. Today the farm, its bakery and its local-produce shop are the beating heart of the Wasven estate.
Een achttiende-eeuwse boerderij op de do: An eighteenth-century farm on the donk, the sandy rise in the stream valley that Karpendonk is named after. The lake beside it was only dug in the twentieth century; the farm was already there.
De molen op de Kleine Dommel, op de gren: The mill on the Kleine Dommel, on the border with Nuenen, is first mentioned in the thirteenth century and was rebuilt in its present form in 1743: a grain mill and an oil mill side by side, each with an undershot wheel. Vincent van Gogh lived in Nuenen in 1884 and 1885 and walked past here; he painted the watermill at Opwetten and the one at Collen, a little upstream.
Een kapelletje van 1954 aan de Loostraat: A little chapel of 1954 on the Loostraat, in the hamlet of 't Coll between the farms and the Kleine Dommel.
Klein Tongelre was een van de gehuchten: Klein Tongelre was one of the hamlets of the municipality of Tongelre, alongside the village core, Urkhoven and 't Coll. This farm and the Veestraat are its oldest traces; the workers' quarter of Lakerlopen grew around them in the 1920s.
Een zeventiende-eeuwse boerderij in Urkh: A seventeenth-century farm in Urkhoven, rebuilt in 1850. Urkhoven is the southernmost hamlet of Tongelre and still a ribbon of farms between the meadows.
Tongelre leefde van de boeren en daarna: Tongelre lived off its farms and then off cigars. The Crielaars factory still stands with the owner's house beside it as it was built in the 1880s, in among the workers' houses of the Lakerstraat.
Van de sigarenindustrie leefden ook de b: The cigar industry also fed the firms that made boxes, matchboxes and cigar bands. The office villa on the corner of the Tongelresestraat and the Dommelhoefstraat is what is left of the cigar-box factory of J. Brüning en zoon, later NV Houtindustrie Picus.
De buurt Lakerlopen heet naar het stroom: The Lakerlopen quarter is named after the Lakerloop, the brook that ran where the Ruysdaelbaan and the Fazantlaan are now. The city architect Louis Kooken designed the quarter around 1920 as social housing for workers: gatehouses, brick fronts and high red roofs. In 2005 much of it was demolished and replaced; the Van Dijckstraat and this gatehouse remain.
Frank van Klingeren bouwde hier in 1973: In 1973 Frank van Klingeren built a neighbourhood building here without walls: school, shops, library and community centre under one big roof, on the idea that people could then not avoid each other. It became world-famous and unbearably noisy; walls were put in later. The roof with its round skylights is still there.
De plas is gegraven voor het zand van he: The lake was dug for the sand that built the railway viaduct joining the north and south of Eindhoven. Around it stands a pine wood with rhododendrons and junipers; there are fish in the water and birdwatchers on the bank.
Een tweede gegraven plas, een halve kilo: A second dug lake, half a kilometre further south, named after the dragline that scooped it out. People swim here in summer; the water is part of the green wedge that runs right through the city.
Het Wasven heet naar het ven waar de sch: The Wasven is named after the fen where sheep were washed before they were shorn. The estate around the Philips farm is now wood, orchard, field and kitchen garden together, run by a foundation with volunteers, with a bakery and a local-produce shop in the farm.
Kasteel Het Borchsken, ook Coudenhove en: Castle Het Borchsken, also called Coudenhove and Beauregard, stood here close to the present guild house of the Sint-Catharinagilde. It was built around 1558 for jonkheer Rutger van Berckel, alderman of 's-Hertogenbosch and lord of Tongelre, and his wife Livina van Coudenhove; her cousin Jacob became chief falconer to the king of Spain in 1585. A document of 1702 speaks of 'the castle with its courtyard and its moats'; in 1705 a great hall, a dining room, a chapel, a kitchen, a little cellar room, a bedroom, a maids' room and a servants' room are named. By 1793 it was badly decayed, and seven years later a hurricane blew the remains down. On the cadastral map only the round moat was still visible.
Deze muur met geglazuurde tegels is het: This wall of glazed tiles is all that is left of the Karel I cigar factory, which stood here until the morning of 19 February 1971, when a fire burned the whole works to the ground. Henri van Abbe began making cigars in Gestel in 1908 and carried on production here from 1915; in 1927 a four-storey industrial complex was added, of which this wall was a part. Van Abbe was one of the largest employers in Eindhoven: in its heyday hundreds of people worked there.
Een gedenksteen met de regel: In trouw o: A memorial stone with the line: Unshakeable in loyalty they bore up the resistance 1940-1944.
Vijf struikelstenen in de stoep voor het: Five brass stones in the pavement in front of the house of the Ekstein family: Aaltje, Esther, Levie, Hartog and Rosa Ekstein-Sleutelberg, who lived here until they were taken away.
Struikelstenen voor Joseph van Vlijmen e: Stones for Joseph van Vlijmen and Bernard André van Vlijmen.
Struikelstenen voor Helena Slijper-van S: Stones for Helena Slijper-van Staveren, Otto Josef Hess and Karl Oettinger.
In 2020 was het honderd jaar geleden dat: In 2020 it was a hundred years since Gestel, Stratum, Strijp, Tongelre and Woensel were joined to Eindhoven. A summer linden was planted in each of those former municipalities to mark it; this one stands in the hamlet of Klein Tongelre. Archaeology tells us the village of Tongelre came into being at the start of the thirteenth century; the oldest records of it are deeds of 1241 and 1244.
Een oud bedrijventerrein aan de Daalakke: An old industrial yard on the Daalakkersweg, built full of studios and workshops of designers and artists; during Dutch Design Week it is packed with visitors.
Uit archeologisch onderzoek weten we dat: Archaeology tells us the village came into being at the start of the thirteenth century, on the high ground along the Dommel. The oldest written records are deeds of 1241 and 1244: Herman Freso Hanegreve gives up his claims to a few properties, and the empress Maria gives her tax income from Tongelre to the convent of Binderen near Helmond. The municipality of Tongelre was this village core and the hamlets of Urkhoven, 't Coll and Klein Tongelre.
Kasteel Het Borchsken, ook Coudenhove en: Castle Het Borchsken, also called Coudenhove and Beauregard, was built around 1558 for jonkheer Rutger van Berckel, alderman of 's-Hertogenbosch and lord of Tongelre, and his wife Livina van Coudenhove. In 1705 a great hall, a dining room, a chapel, a kitchen, a little cellar room, a bedroom, a maids' room and a servants' room are named. By 1793 it was badly decayed; seven years later a hurricane blew the remains down. On the cadastral map only the round moat was still visible.
Een driebeukig hallehuis met een brede m: A three-aisled hall house with a broad middle aisle and two narrow side aisles, house and stable under one roof: one of the oldest buildings in Eindhoven. Around 1600 a raised room with a cellar was added; in the eighteenth century the end wall, the street front and the stable were renewed. The farm stood right on the village square, which has since disappeared. An excavation in 1993 found a refuse pit beside it with seventeenth-century Delftware and stained glass.
De molen op de Kleine Dommel, op de gren: The mill on the Kleine Dommel, on the border with Nuenen, is first mentioned in the thirteenth century and was rebuilt in its present form in 1743: a grain mill and an oil mill side by side, each with an undershot wheel. Vincent van Gogh lived with his parents in Nuenen in 1884 and 1885 and walked past here on his way to Eindhoven; in November 1884 he painted the mill.
Hier stond in 1375 al 'Het goed Ten Hove: 'Het goed Ten Hove' stood here as early as 1375, and in 1637 a brick house called Musberg. Jonkheer Theodorus Smits-van Eckart bought it on 25 September 1846, with all its outbuildings and a farm, and in 1872 had the country house and the farm pulled down and rebuilt larger. Because the complex looked like a castle, it became known as the little castle of Tongelre.
Tongelre had een grote boerenbevolking;: Tongelre was mostly a village of farmers; industry came second, but grew fast. Cigar factories went up along the Lakerstraat and the Tongelresestraat, with the workers' houses right around them. The cigars also fed the firms that made boxes, matchboxes and cigar bands, such as the cigar-box factory of J. Brüning en zoon, later NV Houtindustrie Picus.
Het laatste gemeentehuis van de zelfstan: The last town hall of the independent municipality of Tongelre, to a design by Jan Stuyt. It still stands on the bend of 't Hofke, and is still used for the life of the neighbourhood.
Een driebeukige neogotische kruisbasilie: A three-aisled neo-Gothic cruciform basilica on the spot where Tongelre has gathered round a church since the thirteenth century. The two towers that were to flank the main portal were never finished. On the front of the parsonage beside it stands a Good Shepherd by the Eindhoven sculptor Jan Custers, 1918.
Op 1 januari 1920 werden Tongelre, Strat: On 1 January 1920 Tongelre, Stratum, Gestel, Strijp and Woensel were joined to the small town of Eindhoven, which needed room. Eindhoven had 6,500 inhabitants, Tongelre 3,200. Both the people and the council of Tongelre were against it: they feared higher taxes, a country village swallowed by the city, and more crime. A hundred years later, in 2020, a summer linden was planted as a memorial tree in each of the five former municipalities; Tongelre's stands here, in Klein Tongelre.
De buurt heet naar het stroompje de Lake: The quarter is named after the Lakerloop, the brook that ran where the Ruysdaelbaan and the Fazantlaan are now. The city architect Louis Kooken designed social housing for workers here: gatehouses, brick fronts and high red roofs, with a statue of Saint Joseph as a sign of its Catholic origins. In 2005 much of it was demolished and replaced; the Van Dijckstraat and the gatehouse on the Bosboomstraat remain.
Philips kocht het kasteeltje en de boerd: Philips bought the little castle and the farm in 1920 to build housing. It turned out otherwise: the buildings were only demolished in 1930, and in 1941 Philips put up a farm instead of houses, which stayed in use for a long time. The foundations of the old country house still lie under the grass, surveyed and covered over with sand again. Today the farm, the bakery and the local-produce shop are the heart of the Wasven estate.
Vroeg in de ochtend van 19 februari 1971: Early in the morning of 19 February 1971 fire broke out in the Karel I cigar factory; the whole works burned to the ground. Henri van Abbe had started making cigars in Gestel in 1908 and carried on production here from 1915; in 1927 a four-storey complex was added. He was one of the largest employers in Eindhoven. Only the wall of glazed tiles is still standing.
Frank van Klingeren bouwde hier een wijk: Frank van Klingeren built a neighbourhood building here without walls: school, shops, library and community centre under one big roof, on the idea that people could then not avoid each other. It became world-famous and unbearably noisy; walls were put in after all. The roof with its round skylights is still there.
